candidates.title: Transient reduced-state comparison
candidates.purpose: Determine whether TEA and TEOA produce different transient amplitudes or decay kinetics in the P01 cobalt-containing formulation, while bounding interpretation if donor substitution also changes bulk medium or interfacial properties.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV007 and EV041 support that TEOA can participate in reductive quenching and alter reduced-intermediate lifetimes in photocatalytic systems. EV018 and EV005 support transient methods for donor-sensitive carrier kinetics but also show platform dependence and incomplete species assignment. GX008 supports negative controls and TAS-type characterization in photocatalytic systems. Proposed transfer: compare donor-dependent transient observables in P01 as descriptive kinetic signatures, using no-donor and no-cobalt references and a medium-adjustment pilot to narrow overassignment rather than claiming a specific cobalt intermediate.

comparisons.inference: Primary descriptive contrast for donor-dependent transient amplitudes or lifetimes in the full P01 formulation. A difference supports donor-associated kinetic differences under these conditions but does not by itself identify the transient species or isolate electron-delivery causality.
Tests whether TEOA produces donor-enabled transient populations above the no-donor background.

Compares donor-dependent signals without cobalt. Similar donor trends with and without cobalt shift interpretation toward absorber or support-side carrier dynamics rather than uniquely cobalt-associated kinetics.

Secondary contrast after pilot medium adjustment. If the donor difference persists after narrowing measured bulk-medium differences, support is stronger for donor-associated kinetic effects; if it collapses, the original contrast is bounded by medium confounding.

procedure: Run a pilot to choose sample handling, optical density range, probe wavelengths, and pump fluence that give stable baselines and reproducible donor-enabled signals without obvious damage or nonlinear response.
Acquire transient traces for all groups under matched preparation age, suspension density, optical path, and atmosphere handling, with dark/background subtraction and repeat preparations.

Measure bulk covariates that donor substitution may change, including pH or comparable acidity-basicity readout, absorbance or scattering proxy, and handling observations relevant to suspension behavior, before interpreting kinetic contrasts.

Compare amplitudes and decay parameters only in reproducible time windows with acceptable signal-to-noise, using no-donor and no-cobalt references to keep assignments descriptive unless independently corroborated.

If feasible from the pilot, repeat the TEA versus TEOA comparison under medium-adjusted conditions designed only to narrow measurable bulk differences, then report whether the donor contrast persists, shrinks, or becomes ambiguous.
measurements: Transient absorption or analogous pump-probe amplitude at selected probe wavelengths
Decay kinetics or characteristic lifetimes in reproducible time windows
Dark and no-donor background traces for artifact detection
No-cobalt reference traces to separate cobalt-associated changes from absorber or support-side dynamics
Bulk covariates for each donor condition, including pH or comparable acidity-basicity readout, optical density or scattering proxy, and suspension-handling notes
Assignment confidence statement distinguishing descriptive donor-sensitive transients from specifically assigned cobalt intermediates
candidates.supports: Support for H02 would be a reproducible TEA versus TEOA difference in transient formation, amplitude, or persistence in the full P01 formulation, with donor-enabled signals above no-donor background and a contrast that is absent or smaller in no-cobalt references or that persists after medium-adjustment pilots. This supports donor-associated kinetic differences consistent with altered upstream photoredox delivery, while remaining agnostic about exact intermediate identity unless cross-checked independently.
candidates.refutes: Evidence against a strong upstream donor-kinetics account would be closely matched TEA and TEOA transient observables in cobalt-containing P01 under both baseline and medium-adjusted conditions, provided the method is sensitive enough to detect donor-enabled signals and controls behave as expected. If catalytic selectivity still differs elsewhere under such matched transient behavior, interpretation shifts toward downstream chemistry or unobserved states.
candidates.inconclusive: Inconclusive if signals are too weak, unstable, or dominated by scattering, photothermal artifacts, or degradation; if donor substitution changes bulk-medium properties so strongly that medium-adjusted comparison is not feasible; if no-cobalt references show similar donor differences that cannot be separated from cobalt effects; or if assignments remain too uncertain to connect the transient contrast to the catalytic manifold beyond a descriptive observation.
candidates.parameter_selection: Select probe wavelengths and fitting windows by pilot spectra on donor-containing and no-donor samples, choosing regions with adequate signal-to-noise and minimal artifact. Set pump fluence below nonlinear or damaging regimes by fluence-dependence checks. Keep preparation age, optical density range, and path length matched across groups. If medium adjustment is attempted, choose adjustments only after measuring which bulk properties differ most between TEA and TEOA in the actual samples; do not assume a literature recipe. If adjustment introduces new instability, report only the baseline descriptive comparison.
candidates.limitations: Species assignment in a heterogeneous supported system is provisional, and transient differences do not uniquely prove electron flow into a specific cobalt intermediate. Donor substitution can co-vary pH, viscosity, ionic environment, adsorption, and suspension stability, so even a clear transient difference may reflect combined effects. No-cobalt controls help bound interpretation but do not recreate the same interfacial environment as cobalt-containing samples.

candidates.title: Matched TEA/TEOA photophysics-to-products correlation in the Co-bpy baseline, with optional homogeneous bridge
candidates.purpose: Test whether TEA-versus-TEOA substitution changes donor-side quenching or transient reduced-state observables in the same direction as any CO/H2 shift under otherwise matched conditions, while limiting inference to correlation-versus-discordance rather than causation.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV053 and EV065 support donor-sensitive quenching measurements in cobalt-containing photocatalytic systems, EV007 supports tracking reduced intermediates and CO2-responsive transient behavior in molecular photocatalysis, GX007 shows TEA-for-TEOA substitution can alter irradiation-time photochemistry, and EV081 supports quantifying both CO and H2 with catalyst-omission backgrounds. The proposal transfers these observations into a matched TEA-versus-TEOA comparison in the recommended Co-bpy platform. Any concordance between photophysical and catalytic shifts would remain supportive correlation, not proof that donor-side photophysics is the sole cause of selectivity.

comparisons.inference: Primary single-factor test of whether donor identity shifts both donor-side observables and catalytic CO/H2 outputs under matched P01 conditions.
Checks whether donor substitution changes background photochemistry or H2 formation without cobalt, bounding catalyst-specific interpretation.
Assesses cobalt-dependent contribution under TEOA as a necessity/background contrast, not a donor-side causal test.
Assesses cobalt-dependent contribution under TEA as a necessity/background contrast, not a donor-side causal test.
Optional single-factor donor comparison in the supplementary bridge to test only whether qualitative directionality transfers across platforms, not whether mechanism is shared.

procedure: Verify a chemically matched P01 baseline from the supplied recommendation, then prepare paired TEA and TEOA formulations with all non-donor components, vessel geometry, gas handling, and analytical workflow held fixed; include cobalt-omission controls and use the optional P02 bridge only after P01 matching is demonstrated.

Define and document one pre-measurement history for each measurement block so photophysical samples and catalytic samples are comparable in composition, atmosphere, illumination exposure, and aging; where a sub-mixture is required, justify it against the full mixture with matched blanks and backgrounds.

For each group, collect donor-side photophysical data on the actual mixture or justified sub-mixture: steady-state emission or absorbance behavior suitable for quenching analysis, and a transient optical readout assigned only as a reduced-state or charge-carrier proxy after background subtraction and reference checks.

Run matched photocatalysis on the same formulation family and quantify both CO and H2 with time-resolved sampling if signals exceed detection limits; analyze no-cobalt groups in parallel to estimate donor, photosensitizer, or support background contributions.

Compare donor-dependent photophysical changes against donor-dependent CO/H2 changes across replicate runs, treating agreement as correlation evidence and disagreement as evidence favoring downstream or parallel explanations rather than a direct causal verdict.
measurements: CO amount and H2 amount from the same gas-analysis workflow; derived selectivity reported only as a transformation of measured products, not as a sole readout.

Emission intensity, spectrum, or lifetime changes of the light-absorbing component versus donor identity for matched mixtures or justified sub-mixtures; this reports quenching behavior but cannot alone identify the exact quencher or active intermediate.

Transient absorbance or equivalent time-resolved optical signal assigned to a reduced-state or charge-carrier proxy using references and backgrounds; this can indicate donor-dependent formation or persistence of a transient species but cannot by itself establish the active cobalt state.
Background product formation in cobalt-omission groups to bound donor, photosensitizer, or support contributions.
Documentation of sample-state comparability, including mixture composition, atmosphere, and illumination history for each measurement block.
If the optional bridge is used, the same classes of photophysical readouts and product measurements in P02 to test directionality transfer only.
candidates.supports: H02 is supported if, across matched TEA and TEOA runs in P01, donor substitution reproducibly shifts at least one donor-side quenching or transient observable and catalytic CO/H2 output changes in the same directional sense, while cobalt-omission controls do not account for most of the product shift. Similar qualitative directionality in optional P02 would strengthen plausibility that donor-side behavior contributes, but would still not establish causation or a shared mechanism.
candidates.refutes: H02 is weakened if TEA and TEOA give similar donor-side quenching and transient observables within experimental resolution in P01, yet CO/H2 differs reproducibly beyond the bounded background seen in cobalt-omission controls. That outcome would favor downstream explanations such as proton management, catalyst-state, substrate-binding, or other donor-induced changes not captured by the selected photophysical observables.
candidates.inconclusive: The result is inconclusive if TEA and TEOA formulations cannot be matched reproducibly, if photophysical signals are below assignment confidence or dominated by scattering or support artifacts, if sample-state linkage between photophysics and catalysis is not demonstrated, if background product formation is too large to isolate cobalt-dependent behavior, or if multiple observables shift in inconsistent directions.
candidates.parameter_selection: Do not invent donor concentration, catalyst loading, light intensity, or sampling times. Start from the literature-anchored P01 baseline formulation and verify exact values from the supplied system recommendation. Before the full comparison, run a pilot to choose a dilution window that keeps optical signals measurable without changing component identities, confirms linear detector response, and avoids complete inner-filter saturation. Choose catalytic sampling times by bracketing early, mid, and later illumination intervals where both CO and H2 are above detection and cobalt-omission controls remain interpretable. For each measurement block, first confirm that the defined pre-measurement history yields stable backgrounds and comparable spectra in duplicate preparations. For the optional P02 bridge, first confirm observable quenching in the TEOA formulation before introducing TEA as the single-variable comparator.
candidates.limitations: This design tests correlation versus discordance, not causation. Even reproducible concordance between donor-side observables and CO/H2 does not exclude coupled changes in proton transfer, catalyst speciation, substrate binding, or other downstream chemistry. P01 support effects may decouple measured optical observables from the chemically active manifold. Cobalt-omission contrasts are necessity/background tests because omitting cobalt changes the reaction manifold. The optional P02 bridge improves photophysical interpretability but is not chemically identical to the Co-bpy/g-C3N4 target, so only bounded directionality transfer is justified.

candidates.title: Donor-radical detection under TEA versus TEOA substitution
candidates.purpose: Test whether replacing TEOA with TEA changes detectable donor-derived radical signatures under illumination in a matched cobalt comparison matrix. This is a bounded donor-side characterization experiment, not a direct product-causation test.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV016 reports EPR spin-trapping detection of TEOA-derived radicals and notes similar TEA-derived adducts with TEOA line broadening attributed to viscosity; EV011 supports that both TEA and TEOA can generate alpha-aminoalkyl radical reductants after excited-state quenching; GX018 provides the transferable framework that sacrificial-donor radical cation and radical species can arise in photochemical quenching while their mechanistic role remains uncertain. Proposed transfer: compare TEA and TEOA within one matched cobalt-containing formulation, include donor-matched dark and no-absorber controls, and limit inference to donor-side radical observables.

comparisons.inference: Primary donor-substitution contrast. A reproducible difference in radical-associated signal appearance, spectral pattern, or time profile supports donor-dependent upstream photoredox differences; similar behavior weakens this explanation but does not exclude it.
Tests whether the TEOA radical-associated signal is light-dependent rather than probe background or spontaneous donor oxidation.
Tests whether the TEA radical-associated signal is light-dependent under the same matrix.
Bounds absorber-free background signal for TEOA. If the illuminated no-absorber control shows comparable signal, assignment to absorber-driven photoredox is weakened.
Bounds absorber-free background signal for TEA with the donor held matched.

procedure: Choose the more spectroscopically interpretable matched cobalt formulation by pilot, keeping donor substitution otherwise identical across groups.
Run a short pilot to identify probe loading and irradiation window that give stable baseline and resolvable light-dependent signal above donor-matched dark and no-absorber controls.
Acquire time-matched radical-detection spectra for all groups using identical preparation, irradiation history, and acquisition settings, with TEA and TEOA runs interleaved to reduce drift bias.
Compare signal presence, line shape, linewidth, and time evolution across donor substitution while checking donor-matched controls before making any assignment.
If a donor difference appears, relate it conservatively to linked quenching or transient experiments rather than treating one trapped-radical feature as proof of the productive catalytic route.
measurements: EPR or equivalent radical-detection spectra for illuminated, dark, and no-absorber donor-matched samples
Signal presence or absence relative to donor-matched backgrounds
Line shape and linewidth, explicitly noting possible viscosity or motion effects
Time-dependent growth and decay of radical-associated signals under matched irradiation and acquisition windows
If feasible, parallel absorber integrity check by optical spectroscopy
candidates.supports: Support for H02 would be a reproducible donor-substitution effect under matched conditions in which TEA and TEOA differ in radical-associated signal behavior, both illuminated donor-containing samples exceed their donor-matched dark controls, and donor-matched no-absorber controls remain clearly smaller.
candidates.refutes: Evidence against H02 as a dominant explanation would be closely similar TEA and TEOA radical-detection behavior across repeated matched runs with clean light dependence and low donor-matched background, especially if linked quenching observables are also similar while catalysis still diverges.
candidates.inconclusive: Inconclusive outcomes include no resolved signal for either donor, strong probe or background chemistry, severe overlap or broadening preventing assignment, absorber instability during acquisition, or donor differences comparable to donor-matched no-absorber backgrounds. A radical-associated signal alone does not establish productive catalysis or control of CO versus H2.
candidates.parameter_selection: Do not fix donor loading, probe concentration, or irradiation time from unrelated systems. Use pilot series to choose the lowest probe level giving a stable baseline and the shortest acquisition window that resolves a light-dependent signal without obvious bleaching or runaway background. After calibration, keep solvent matrix, atmosphere, irradiation geometry, and acquisition settings identical across TEA and TEOA.
candidates.limitations: Radical trapping can perturb chemistry, and detected adducts may be secondary trapped products rather than the immediate quenching intermediate. TEA and TEOA can differ in viscosity and line broadening, so spectral differences are not automatically identity differences. If only a supplementary readable platform works, transfer back to the main catalytic platform remains limited. This experiment does not measure CO or H2.
